column3: BSB moves the command ahead of the comparison; the Greek presents the comparison first.
“To them” supplies objects for doing good and lending that are not separately stated.
“Forgive” expresses the contextual sense of the verb literally meaning release.
The Greek has an indefinite active plural “they will give”; BSB uses the passive “will be poured.”
The Greek explicitly says “to your brother” before the address; BSB leaves that recipient implicit.
BSB’s “man” and “treasure of his heart” in the evil person’s clause match the Textus Receptus (θησαυροῦ); the critical text does not repeat them.
BSB moves “I will show you” ahead of the description of the person.
“My words” and “on them” supply objects not explicitly repeated in the Greek.
